title: When the ZIA Terraform provider reports success after an error, or crashes
aliases: terraform refresh succeeds but api failed
terraform destroy succeeded but rule still in state

checks.do: Whether a clean refresh or apply actually read these settings, by re-reading them from the API, since a failed read returns no error.
Whether a rule was posted twice after a create that took unusually long or errored: list the rules by name and look for a second copy or an unmanaged first one.
Whether a failed parent or subrule read happened earlier in the run, when DLP web rule creates hang or a subrule create crashes the provider.

not-found-destroy-keeps-id.statement: When the DLP web rule delete call fails with RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, Delete treats the rule as already gone and returns `nil` diagnostics, which Terraform accepts as a successful destroy. That is the right outcome; the one difference from the success path is that it returns before the activation step, so nothing triggers activation for this destroy.

create-reposts-after-read-error.statement: In DLP web rule create, after the POST succeeds and the ID is set, a Read that returns an error diagnostic makes the create loop sleep and `continue` while time remains in the create timeout. The next loop pass calls `Create` again with the same request; the object from the first POST is not looked up or adopted before it.

duplicate-post-result.statement: A second POST of the same rule may create a duplicate policy rule, or may be rejected (for example on a name clash), leaving the first rule created but the apply failing. The code shows only that the second POST is sent.
duplicate-post-result.conditions: Depends on how the ZIA API treats a second create with an identical name and body: duplicates are allowed, or it is refused. Not tested (gap duplicate-post-response).

empty-body-panic-sites.statement: The unchecked assertion followed by a field read is in about 68 SDK service functions across about 66 files, mostly each service's Update. Among them are the services behind the provider's admin roles, alerts, bandwidth control, CASB rules, DLP web rules, endpoint DLP, firewall and DNS rules, forwarding, IPS, location management, NAT control, sandbox rules, SSL inspection, traffic capture, GRE tunnels, static IPs, VPN credentials, URL categories, users, VZEN and workload group resources.
empty-body-panic-sites.conditions: Found by a regex over zscaler/zia/services/**/*.go (`x, _ := y.(*T)` where `x.<field>` is read within 400 characters) on a `git archive` of sdk-go at v3.8.44 and at HEAD; both return the same 68 matches in 66 files (a few are not on a provider resource update path, for example EUSA status and make-default certificate). The matches do not prove each provider resource reaches its function with an empty body, only that the function cannot handle one. Whether the ZIA API ever answers these updates with an empty body is gap rule-update-empty-body in zia.sdk-go.write-encoding.

upstream.note: Filing 5 (success-shaped errors and panics) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

dlp-web-lock-not-released-on-error.statement: Inside that locked section, a failed Get of any subrule returns the error directly, and the panic above also unwinds, without releasing `dlpWebRulesLock`. The lock is released only by one explicit `Unlock` later in the loop body. Every later DLP web rule create (parent or subrule) then blocks on the same lock for the life of the provider process.

dlp-web-lock-not-released-on-error.conditions: Rests on an absence: `grep -n dlpWebRulesLock zia/resource_zia_dlp_web_rules.go` at tf-zia v4.8.3 and HEAD shows the declaration, one Lock and one Unlock, with no `defer`. A panic inside a provider normally ends the process, so the held lock matters in practice for the error return and for a host that recovers panics.

update-parks-at-last-rule-order.statement: In the sandbox rules and firewall DNS rules update paths, the order of the last rule in the sorted list of existing rules is taken as `nextAvailableOrder`, and the rule is then updated with rank 7 and that order, so it is parked at the end of the policy before the reorder helper is called. The same three-line sequence follows the same index in the other rule resources listed under the index-panic claim.

empty-reply-panic-follows-server-answer.statement: The nil dereference on an empty update reply happens after the SDK has received the server's answer to the PUT, so the panic cannot undo a change the server has already applied.
empty-reply-panic-follows-server-answer.conditions: Assumes the empty body arrives with a success status such as 204, which is the case the helper treats as a nil result with a nil error; whether any ZIA update endpoint answers that way is open (gap zia.sdk-go.write-encoding:rule-update-empty-body).
